title: Why double-checked locking needs volatile, and why enums resist reflection

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A double-checked locking Singleton declares its instance field without volatile. What can go wrong?

options.text: Two threads can both pass the check made under the lock and each build an instance.
options.says: The second check runs while the lock is held, so only one thread can find the field null there and construct.

options.text: A thread can read a non-null reference to an object whose constructor has not finished.
options.says: Without volatile the write of the reference may be reordered before the constructor's writes, so the unlocked first check can see a partly built object.

options.text: Every call to getInstance() takes the lock, so the pattern loses its speed advantage.
options.says: The first check runs without the lock whatever the field's modifiers are; volatile changes visibility and ordering, not when the lock is taken.

questions.stem: Code gets the private constructor of an enum Singleton, calls setAccessible(true) and then newInstance(). What happens?

options.text: It returns a second constant unless the constructor checks a flag of its own.
options.says: An enum needs no flag: the JVM itself refuses to instantiate enum types reflectively.

options.text: It returns the existing INSTANCE, the way readResolve does after deserialization.
options.says: readResolve is a serialization hook; reflective construction of an enum does not return anything, it fails.

options.text: It throws IllegalArgumentException, because the JVM forbids creating enum objects that way.
options.says: Constructor.newInstance on an enum type throws IllegalArgumentException, which is why the enum Singleton is reflection-safe.

concepts: The JVM refuses to create an enum constant reflectively, so Constructor.newInstance on an enum throws IllegalArgumentException.
Double-checked locking needs a volatile field, because without it another thread can see a reference to a partly constructed object.
